welcome.title: Welcome, {{name}}
welcome.subtitle: This is where you find out how your database holds up under load: Stroppy Cloud brings it up in your cloud, runs a scenario like TPC-C and shows how many queries per second it handled and at what latency.
welcome.verifyBody: We mailed you a code. If someone invited you to a tenant, the invite applies right after you confirm.
welcome.notInvited: Nobody invited me. Create my tenant
welcome.invitedTitle: You are already on a team:
welcome.createBody: A tenant holds everything your team does: tests, runs, cloud keys and the member list. Create one and connect a cloud; you can invite colleagues later.
welcome.demo: See what a result looks like

database.title: Database
database.body: What you're testing: the DBMS, its version and how the nodes connect.
database.more: The database you want to test: PostgreSQL, MySQL, YDB, CockroachDB and more, its version, topology (one node, replicas, a Patroni or Galera cluster) and settings. Describe it once and drop it into any test after that.

workload.title: Workload
workload.body: How you load it: the scenario, the number of users and how long.
workload.more: A load scenario, for example “load the TPC-C data, then run 64 virtual users for 10 minutes”. A workload isn't tied to a database, so you can run the same one on PostgreSQL and on MySQL and compare them fairly.

test.title: Test
test.body: What you launch: a database, a workload and machine sizes.
test.more: A test ties a database to a workload and says which machines to run them on: how much CPU and memory the database nodes and the runner get. Before you launch, Stroppy Cloud checks the machines are big enough and suggests sizes if they aren't.

run.title: Run
run.body: One run of a test: the stand, the load, the result.
run.more: Every press of Launch creates a run. Stroppy Cloud brings up the stand in your cloud, installs and checks the database and drives the load, while you watch logs, metrics and QPS in the console.

facts.label: Stand
items: can be kept for a while

results.title: Results
results.body: How many queries per second the database handled, and at what latency.
results.more: A run leaves a report: QPS, latency, errors and charts for each segment. You can compare it with other runs, send it to the rating or open it for colleagues by a public link.

suite.title: Suite
suite.body: Several variants of a test at once, to compare them.
suite.more: A suite is for questions like “which is faster”: PostgreSQL 16 or 17, S machines or M. You list the variants, the suite runs them all and puts the results in one table.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.body: Launches a test on its own, on cron.
schedule.more: Every night at 03:00, say. That way you notice a new version or new database settings got slower before production does; each of those runs leaves an ordinary report.

provider.title: Provider
provider.body: Your cloud account, where the machines come up.
provider.more: A key to your Yandex Cloud account (AWS soon). Stroppy Cloud creates machines there for the length of a run and removes them afterwards; the cloud bills you for them directly.

tenant.title: Tenant
tenant.body: Your team's space; everything else lives in it.
tenant.more: A tenant groups people and their work: members with roles, cloud keys, the library of databases and workloads, runs and limits. Different teams work in different tenants and can't see each other.

concepts.hint: Hover a block to read what it is for.

tests.title: Tests
tests.body: This is where benchmarks start: each test already knows which database, which workload and which machines to use.

runs.title: Runs
runs.body: Every run of every test. While a run is going you see its logs and metrics here, and once it's done the report is here too.

databases.title: Databases
databases.body: The DBMS setups you're testing. Tests take their database from here.

workloads.title: Workloads
workloads.body: Load scenarios: what to do to the database and for how long.

suites.title: Suites
suites.body: Sets of variants of one test, compared with one button.

examples.title: Examples
examples.body: Ready tests that already work. Clone an example and launch it to see what a result looks like straight away.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Cloud keys, team members, limits and webhooks.

search.title: Search
search.body: Finds runs, tests and databases by name; press / to open it.

tenant.title: Tenant
tenant.body: Switch between teams here, or create a new one.

userMenu.title: Your menu
userMenu.body: Profile, theme and language. You can replay this tour from here too.

empty.runs: Runs show up here once you launch a test or a suite. Each one brings up a stand in your cloud, drives the load and leaves a report.
empty.tests: A test says which database to check, under which load and on which machines. The easiest start is an example: it's already set up and launches right away.
empty.databases: This is where you keep the databases you test: engine, version, topology and configs. You can also define a database right inside a test, but keeping it here lets several tests share it.
empty.workloads: A workload says what to do to the database, for example load the TPC-C data and run queries for 10 minutes. The same workload runs on different databases.
empty.suites: A suite runs several variants of a test at once, say three PostgreSQL versions on two machine sizes, and puts the results in one table.
empty.schedules: A schedule launches a test or a suite on cron by itself, every night for example, so you catch a slowdown before your users do.
